sources.title: Southern Bug River: water security and climate changes perspectives for post-war city of Mykolaiv, Ukraine
sources.organization: Snizhko et al., Frontiers in Water
sources.temporal_coverage: Water-supply disruption from April 2022; water-quality conditions reported in the study; hydrological projections for near-future 2021–2050 and far-future 2051–2080.
sources.methodology: WaterGAP2 flow and climate-model ensemble assessment under SSP1-2.6 and SSP5-8.5.
sources.limitations: Separates wartime damage from modeled risks to a proposed replacement; projections are not observed.

sources.title: Water quality in the Dnipro–Donbas canal (Ukraine) under conditions of war and climate change
sources.temporal_coverage: Monitoring observations from 2015–2024; discussion of post-2023 infrastructure changes; author projection to 2050.
sources.methodology: Original canal-water study using official monitoring observations from 2015–2024 and irrigation-water quality indicators.
sources.limitations: Only three sampling campaigns per growing season; the authors say this misses short-term salinity peaks and represents background or seasonal-average conditions.

sources.title: UNDP Ukraine Annual Report 2025: Resilient Recovery and Inclusive Development
geographic_coverage: 22 cities participating in municipal solar-energy contracts
sources.temporal_coverage: UNDP-reported programme activities and results during 2025; report published 22 April 2026.
sources.methodology: Annual implementation report summarizing reported 2025 UNDP energy, recovery and service-support activities.
sources.limitations: Implementer-reported outputs; the report does not provide a counterfactual or isolate climate-adaptation effects.

sources.title: Розподілена генерація в Україні: як децентралізовані рішення допомагають тримати тепло та водопостачання в умовах війни
sources.organization: Ministry for Communities and Territories Development of Ukraine
sources.temporal_coverage: Government-reported commissioning and support through 4 January 2026; includes 2025 implementation figures and 2026 plans.
sources.methodology: Ministry news page describing reported distributed-energy commissioning and support for heat, water and other critical services.
sources.limitations: National aggregate figures without named-hromada allocation; operational capability statements are not independent service-outcome evaluations.

claims.locator: Section 1, paragraph describing the April 2022 damage to the Dnipro–Mykolaiv pipeline.
claims.paraphrase: Military operations destroyed Mykolaiv’s Dnipro intake on 12 April 2022, cutting drinking water to the city’s roughly 470,000 residents.
claims.limitations: A conflict-related service loss, not climate-attributed.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Military operations destroyed the intake and cut city water.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: Section 1, paragraph describing the April 2022 destruction and supply interruption.

claims.locator: Section 2.1, paragraphs on alternative wells and water delivery to remote parts of Mykolaiv.
claims.paraphrase: By 2024, remote-area wells yielded 5,000–10,000 m³/day against pre-war demand of at least 80,000; reported quality exceeded drinking-water limits and water was trucked daily.

claims.locator: Sections 2.3.1–2.3.2 and 3, modeled flow results for the proposed Southern Bug supply.
claims.paraphrase: For a proposed Southern Bug supply, May–October withdrawals reach 40–79% of modeled flow in 2051–2080 under SSP5-8.5, highest in low-flow months.
claims.scenario: SSP5-8.5; far-future 2051–2080, as specified by the authors.
claims.limitations: Modeled risk for a proposed alternative, not observed shortage.

claims.locator: Abstract and section 2.1, study-area description after the 2023 Kakhovka destruction.
claims.paraphrase: The study says the 2023 Kakhovka destruction increased the Dnipro–Donbas canal’s importance as a water and food-security route for Ukraine’s steppe zone.
claims.limitations: The source describes a changed post-destruction role; it does not quantify local household water losses.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The authors state that after the 2023 Kakhovka destruction the canal became a key water and food-security artery for the steppe zone.

claims.locator: Abstract and section 5, conclusions on monitoring results and combined pressures.
claims.paraphrase: From 2015–2024, up to one-quarter of sampled canal water during low-flow periods was classed as only limited-suitability irrigation water; the authors attribute salinity changes to low flows, evaporation and combined climate and infrastructure pressures.
institutions: Regional Water Resources Office in Dnipropetrovsk Region
claims.limitations: The paper describes combined pressures but does not quantify the separate contribution of climate versus infrastructure disruption; monitoring is seasonally sparse.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The authors describe water-quality transformation as arising from the synergy of climate change and infrastructure disruption.

claims.locator: Printed p. 12, energy-services results and municipal solar contracts.
claims.paraphrase: UNDP reports 30 municipal ESCO solar contracts across 22 cities, totalling 5.1 MW and intended to serve 541,000 people; it says these installations eased pressure on damaged grids and helped maintain services during attacks and outages.
claims.limitations: The report does not name the 22 cities or independently evaluate service continuity; this is not presented as a climate-adaptation outcome.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: UNDP says the solar contracts eased pressure on damaged grids and helped services continue through attacks and outages.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: Printed p. 12, municipal energy support and ESCO contract paragraphs.

claims.locator: Printed p. 12, energy recovery results paragraph.
claims.paraphrase: UNDP reports energy equipment support that restored or maintained services for more than 6.6 million people; it also says attacks delayed commissioning of several units.
affected_groups: people reliant on supported energy services
claims.limitations: UNDP-reported reach is national and not disaggregated by locality; it does not estimate the attacks’ causal effect on service outcomes.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: UNDP reports that attacks delayed commissioning of several supplied energy units.

claims.locator: Paragraphs on distributed generation commissioned and municipal heat/water operation.
claims.paraphrase: The ministry reported that more than 570 MW of new public-sector distributed-generation capacity had been commissioned by January 2026; it says modular boilers and co-generation can operate near users when large facilities are damaged or de-energized.
institutions: Ministry for Communities and Territories Development
claims.limitations: The capacity total is national; the article does not provide named local allocations or independently measured continuity outcomes.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The ministry says decentralized systems help maintain heat and water when large facilities are damaged or de-energized during attacks.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: Opening paragraphs and section on distributed-generation commissioning.

claims.locator: Paragraph on 2025 support for frontline oblasts.
claims.paraphrase: The ministry says UAH 665 million was allocated in 2025 to frontline oblasts for fuel supporting municipal and critical-infrastructure operation.
institutions: Ministry for Communities and Territories Development
claims.limitations: The release does not identify recipient oblasts or report service outcomes attributable to the fuel support.

search_audit.query: Ukraine oblast district local climate vulnerability drought floods 2024 2025 2026 official climate adaptation assessment
search_audit.outcome: Found directly read Mykolaiv water-supply research and Dnipro–Donbas canal monitoring. Regional Mykolaiv climate-assessment PDFs were listed but unreadable; no claims were taken from their metadata.

search_audit.query: Ukraine climate conflict water security climate change war destroyed water supply local city adaptation primary study
search_audit.outcome: The Mykolaiv article separately identifies military destruction of the former supply and models climate risk to a proposed replacement; the canal study explicitly describes combined climate and infrastructure pressures. No claim makes climate the cause of wartime violence.

search_audit.query: Ukraine conflict inhibits municipal climate adaptation access mines shelling local adaptation plans report primary
search_audit.outcome: Directly read UNDP and ministry sources document attacks delaying energy-unit commissioning and conflict-related infrastructure disruptions; no inspected source established that violence blocked a named local climate-adaptation project.

search_audit.query: Ukraine municipal hromada local climate resilience capacity outcomes decentralized energy adaptation recovery 2025 2026 official report
search_audit.outcome: UNDP reports municipal solar contracts; the ministry reports nationwide distributed-generation commissioning and frontline-oblast support. Mykolaiv climate-risk PDFs and a 2026 resilience-atlas page were not accessible as substantive text.

gaps: Mykolaiv's 2024 and 2025 regional climate-risk PDFs were listed by the official regional page but their substantive text was inaccessible; no findings are inferred from their metadata.
The Dnipro–Donbas paper reports sparse sampling (three campaigns per growing season), so short salinity peaks may be missed.

No inspected new source establishes a named violence-to-climate-adaptation interruption; conflict-related water and energy damage is reported separately from climate pressures except where the canal authors explicitly describe combined pressures.
Municipal solar and distributed-generation evidence is national or multi-city aggregate; named-city allocation and independent service-continuity evaluation are not provided.
